verbalization: Euphorbol is linked to LS174T through a series of molecular interactions involving the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex, which serves as a target for multiple compounds. The evidence suggests that Euphorbol acts as a ligand for this complex, potentially modulating its activity. The presence of two distinct compounds—(2,3,6-trihydroxy-4,5-dimethoxy-7-methyl-10-oxo-9H-anthracen-9-yl) decanoate and (3S,3aS,8aR)-8a-methyl-3-prop-1-en-2-yl-2,3,3a,4,5,8-hexahydro-1H-azulene-6-carboxylic acid—indicates that Euphorbol may interact with the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex in a manner that influences the activity of the complex, which in turn affects LS174T. The integration of these pathways highlights a potential mechanism by which Euphorbol modulates the function of the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex, ultimately influencing LS174T. The evidence supports a role for Euphorbol in targeting the EZH2/SUZ12/EED complex, which is a key player in epigenetic regulation, and this interaction may be central to the mechanism by which Euphorbol affects LS174T.
